## Project Overview

Developer-first, white-label application-email platform — a Resend competitor. **Transactional first** (the acute developer pain point), **marketing/lifecycle later** on the same event stream. Drop-in Resend-compatible API + deliverability suite + white-label multi-tenancy.

Full strategy & product context: `.bootspring/context/` (VISION, AUDIENCE, MARKET, COMPETITORS, BUSINESS_MODEL, PRD, ARCHITECTURE, DELIVERABILITY, INFRA, ROADMAP, RESEARCH, DECISIONS). First feature spec: `.bootspring/specs/transactional-core/`.

## Critical Constraints (read before coding)

- **License boundary (DECISIONS D1):** build on **freeresend (MIT)**; treat **usesend (AGPLv3) as clean-room inspiration only**. NEVER copy usesend source into this proprietary product.
- **Resend compatibility is the wedge:** the public API must accept Resend's payloads/responses so the `resend` SDK works with only a base-URL change. Add features as a superset; don't break compat.
- **Multi-tenant from the schema up:** every resource is scoped to a project under an org. No cross-tenant access — enforce at the data layer, not the UI.
- **Deliverability is non-negotiable:** authenticated-domain sends must reach the inbox; suppression is enforced pre-send; abuse screening ships in Phase 1, not later.
- **Provider seam:** all sending goes through `MailProvider` (`packages/providers`). SES is v1; never hardcode SES outside that package.

## Repo Layout (pnpm monorepo)

```
apps/dashboard   Next.js control panel (Phase 1a)
apps/api         Hono Resend-compatible public API
apps/workers     BullMQ processors (send, webhooks, events)
packages/db      Prisma schema + client (control plane)
packages/providers  MailProvider interface + SesProvider
packages/core    queue, env, Resend zod schema, errors
infra/           docker-compose (local pg+redis), deploy notes
```

## Deployment (real fleet — see .bootspring/context/INFRA.md)

- **Hub box .223** (`31.220.104.223`) — **hostssh** (our own platform; Coolify retired). ems runs here. **Deploy: `git push hostssh main`** (remote → `ssh://root@31.220.104.223/srv/hostssh/ems.git`). One Dockerfile builds a single image; the post-receive hook deploys api (default CMD, blue-green) then `hostssh deploy --command` siblings for web (`pnpm --filter @ems/web start`) and workers (`pnpm --filter @ems/workers start`), each with its own env-file (`/srv/hostssh/ems/{env,env-web,env-workers}`).
- **Data box .211** (`31.220.104.211`) — Postgres 18 + pgvector at `10.10.0.2:5432` (PgBouncer `:6432`); shared **Valkey** at `10.10.0.2:6379` for BullMQ; shared MinIO `10.10.0.2:9000`.
- **Cloudflare** — DNS (`Zone:DNS:Edit` token), R2, edge. electronicmailservices.com cutover DNS-only + LE.
- **AWS** — no standing infra; provision SES via the AWS API MCP; request production access early.

## Development Guidelines

- TypeScript everywhere; Zod for all input validation.
- Dashboard: Server Components by default; Server Actions / tRPC for mutations.
- Keep files focused (< ~300 lines); follow existing patterns.
- Never expose API keys client-side; keys stored hashed; sensitive payload fields encrypted at rest.
- Write tests for new behavior; the SC-001 e2e "definition of trust" is the Phase 1 launch gate.

## Git Commits (fleet convention)

- Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`. Atomic.
- **Never add Co-Authored-By or AI attribution** (matches the Girard Media fleet convention used across servoagent and the other apps).
- Never commit secrets, `.env` real values, or overwrite migrations.
